question: Ari controls [Magus of the Moon] enchanted with [Ichthyomorphosis]. Is Ari's [Dormant Volcano] a Mountain?
answer:
Yes. Ari's Dormant Volcano is a Mountain.

Why: type-changing effects (layer 4) are applied before ability-removing effects (layer 6), regardless of which effect began first [613.1d], [613.6]. Magus of the Moon's ability "Nonbasic lands are Mountains" is applied in layer 4, so even though Ichthyomorphosis makes Magus of the Moon lose all abilities, the subtype-setting effect still applies [Magus of the Moon ruling #0].

Consequences for Dormant Volcano:
- It is a land with the land type Mountain, and it loses its other land types and its own rules-text abilities — so no "enters tapped," no enters-the-battlefield sacrifice trigger, and no "{T}: Add {C}{R}" [305.7], [Magus of the Moon ruling #4].
- Instead it gains the intrinsic Mountain mana ability "{T}: Add {R}" — note that's one red mana, not {C}{R} [305.7], [Magus of the Moon ruling #4].
- It is not a basic land and keeps its name and any supertypes; Magus of the Moon doesn't touch names or supertypes [205.4b], [Magus of the Moon ruling #1].

Side note on Magus of the Moon itself: Ichthyomorphosis makes it a blue Fish with base power and toughness 0/1 that has lost all abilities, but it's still a creature, so the Aura stays attached [Ichthyomorphosis ruling #5].

This works the same at any table size — Magus of the Moon affects all nonbasic lands, so with more than two players every opponent's nonbasic lands are Mountains too.

question: Averie controls [Muraganda Petroglyphs] and [Wayward Angel], and has more than 7 cards in their graveyard. Nathan casts and resolves [Humility]. What are Wayward Angel's characteristics?
answer:
Wayward Angel ends up a 6/6 black Angel Horror creature with no abilities (still controlled by Averie, still named Wayward Angel, mana cost {4}{W}{W}).

How the layers get there (CR 613.1, 613.2c):

- Layer 5 (color): Wayward Angel's threshold ability (timestamp earlier than Humility) makes it black — and only black, not white and black (Wayward Angel ruling #0).
- Layer 6 (abilities): The threshold ability first grants trample and the upkeep-sacrifice trigger; then Humility, with the later timestamp, removes all abilities from all creatures. Wayward Angel ends layer 6 with no abilities at all — no flying, vigilance, trample, upkeep trigger, or the threshold ability itself.
- Layer 7b (setting P/T): Humility sets base power and toughness to 1/1.
- Layer 7c (modifying P/T): The threshold ability's +3/+3 still applies. Per CR 613.6, an effect that has started applying in one layer (here, the color change in layer 5) continues to apply in every other applicable layer even though the ability generating it was removed in layer 6 — the same principle the Humility/Opalescence ruling illustrates (Humility ruling #2). So 1/1 becomes 4/4.
- Layer 7c continued: Muraganda Petroglyphs gives +2/+2 to creatures with no abilities. Because Humility stripped Wayward Angel's abilities in layer 6, it genuinely has no abilities when Muraganda Petroglyphs is checked, so it gets +2/+2 (CR 113.12 — being black or having set P/T isn't an ability). 4/4 becomes 6/6.

Assumption on timing: Humility resolved after Wayward Angel and Muraganda Petroglyphs were already on the battlefield, so Humility has the latest timestamp. If instead Humility had the earlier timestamp than Wayward Angel's threshold effect (not possible here as described), the 7b set-to-1/1 would apply after the +3/+3 and you'd get 1/1 + 2/2 from Muraganda Petroglyphs = 3/3.

Player count doesn't matter: Humility affects all creatures regardless of controller, and Muraganda Petroglyphs affects all abilityless creatures, so the answer is the same at a two-player or multiplayer table. Note Averie's graveyard count keeps threshold's condition satisfied, but even if it stopped being satisfied the ability is gone anyway once layer 6 applies.

question: Nico controls [Urza's Saga] with two lore counters on it. Alexzander uses [Jinx] to change its land type. What happens?
answer:
Urza's Saga is immediately sacrificed. Alexzander's Jinx sets Urza's Saga's land subtype to a basic land type of Alexzander's choice (say Island), which means Urza's Saga loses all abilities generated from its rules text and gains that basic land's mana ability (305.7). That strips away its chapter abilities (I, II, and III) and its Saga-defining chapter text.

But Jinx only replaces subtypes from the land-type set (205.1a, 305.7) — the Saga subtype is an enchantment type, and the card's Enchantment Land card types aren't changed either, so Urza's Saga is still an Enchantment Land — Saga Island with two lore counters. A Saga with no chapter abilities and no remaining chapters to trigger is put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action; this is exactly the scenario the official ruling covers: "If Urza's Saga loses all of its chapter abilities but is still a Saga, perhaps due to a card like Blood Moon, it will immediately be sacrificed" (Urza's Saga ruling #1). Note the ruling wording — Nico sacrifices it — and card/ruling text governs here.

Two details: the lore counters stay on the permanent even though they no longer do anything meaningful (205.1a), and abilities granted to Urza's Saga by other effects would survive Jinx (305.7) — but here chapters I and II granted their abilities to Urza's Saga itself from its own rules text, so per ruling #5 those granted abilities existed, and regardless the permanent is sacrificed right away, so nothing is left to use. Nico gets no chapter III search.

Timing assumption: I'm assuming Urza's Saga is on the battlefield with two lore counters and Jinx resolves before its third chapter trigger would be put on the stack (i.e., not during Nico's draw step with a chapter III trigger already waiting). If a chapter III trigger were already on the stack, that trigger exists independently on the stack and would still resolve and search, while Urza's Saga itself is sacrificed as a state-based action as soon as Jinx resolves.

This works the same at a two-player table or in multiplayer; nothing here depends on the number of players.

question: Aaden activates [Inkmoth Nexus], equips [Colossus Hammer] to it, then activates Inkmoth Nexus again. What are the characteristics of Inkmoth Nexus?
answer:
Inkmoth Nexus ends up as an 11/11 colorless Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature land with flying and infect (plus its own two activated abilities), equipped with Colossus Hammer.

How the layers get there (CR 613.6, 613.7):

- Layer 4 (types): both activations of Inkmoth Nexus's ability make it an artifact creature Phyrexian Blinkmoth that's still a land; "still a land" means it keeps its prior card types (CR 205.1b). Supertypes are unaffected (CR 205.4b) — Inkmoth Nexus has none.
- Layer 5 (color): Inkmoth Nexus's ability doesn't name a color, so it stays colorless.
- Layer 6 (abilities), in timestamp order: first activation grants flying and infect; then Colossus Hammer's "loses flying" removes flying; then the second activation (latest timestamp) grants flying and infect again. Net result: it has both flying and infect. Colossus Hammer only strips flying once, at its own timestamp — it doesn't keep re-removing later-granted flying.
- Layer 7b (setting P/T): both activations set base power and toughness to 1/1; the later one wins, so base 1/1.
- Layer 7c (modifying P/T): Colossus Hammer's +10/+10 applies, giving 11/11.

Note on Colossus Hammer staying attached: Inkmoth Nexus is a creature the whole time here, so Colossus Hammer remains legally attached (CR 301.5c) — the state-based action that unattaches Equipment from an illegal permanent (CR 704.1) never triggers. Also, while Inkmoth Nexus is a creature it still has its mana ability, but summoning-sickness restrictions apply: if it hasn't been under Aaden's control since his most recent turn began, it can't attack or be tapped for mana while it's a creature (Inkmoth Nexus rulings #0 and #1).

Timing assumption: I'm assuming the stated order — activate, then equip, then activate again — which is what makes the second activation's later timestamp restore flying. If Colossus Hammer's equip resolved last instead, flying would be removed at the latest timestamp and Inkmoth Nexus would be an 11/11 with infect but no flying. Nothing here depends on the number of players; the answer is the same in two-player and multiplayer games.

question: Ari casts [Aeve, Progenitor Ooze], with two spells having been cast before then. Nadia controls [Humility]. What will Ari's battlefield look like once the stack fully resolves and state-based actions are checked?
answer:
Ari ends up with three green Ooze creatures: two nonlegendary Aeve, Progenitor Ooze tokens that are 1/1 and 2/2, plus the real (legendary) Aeve, Progenitor Ooze at 3/3 — all three with no abilities. Nothing dies and the legend rule doesn't trim anything.

How that happens:

1. Storm: casting Aeve, Progenitor Ooze with two spells cast earlier this turn copies it twice; per Aeve, Progenitor Ooze's own reminder text the copies become tokens. Copies of a spell are themselves spells put on the stack (707.10e, 707.2), and they resolve first, then the original (Aeve, Progenitor Ooze ruling #2).
2. Counters still get placed. Humility only removes abilities from creatures on the battlefield; a permanent that is entering is not yet there, so "Aeve enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each other Ooze you control" — a replacement effect (614.1) — still applies as each one enters. Per Aeve, Progenitor Ooze ruling #2, assuming Ari controlled no other Oozes to start: token #1 enters with 0 counters, token #2 with 1, and the original Aeve, Progenitor Ooze with 2. Humility doesn't change subtypes, so each one is still an Ooze for the count.
3. Layers (CR 613, as run): Layer 4 — "Aeve isn't legendary if it's a token" applies to the two tokens, stripping Legendary; because it already started applying it isn't undone by Humility later (Humility ruling #2 / 613.6). Layer 6 — Humility removes all abilities from all three. Layer 7b — Humility sets base power/toughness 1/1. Layer 7c — +1/+1 counters apply after Humility's base-setting, so: token #1 = 1/1, token #2 = 2/2, original Aeve, Progenitor Ooze = 3/3.
4. State-based actions: no creature has 0 toughness, and only one of the three is Legendary, so the legend rule doesn't apply.

Timing note: I'm assuming the two prior spells were both cast this turn before Aeve, Progenitor Ooze and that Humility was already on the battlefield the whole time. If Humility instead arrived after the Oozes, the printed 2/2 bodies plus counters would have been 2/2, 3/3, 4/4 before Humility, and once Humility resolves it would still set base 1/1 with counters on top, giving the same 1/1, 2/2, 3/3 result. question: Natalie controls [High Fae Trickster]. Allen activates the crew ability of [Capenna Express]. Before it resolves Natalie casts [One with the Stars] targeting Capenna Express. What happens when the crew ability resolves?
answer:
Short answer: Natalie can't legally cast One with the Stars targeting Capenna Express at that moment, so the crew ability resolves normally and Capenna Express becomes an artifact creature (6/6) until end of turn.

Why: Crew 3 on Capenna Express means "Tap any number of other untapped creatures you control with total power 3 or greater: This permanent becomes an artifact creature until end of turn" [702.122a]. While that activated ability is still on the stack, Capenna Express has not yet become a creature — it's just an artifact Vehicle with no power or toughness [208.3a], [301.7]. One with the Stars says "Enchant creature or enchantment," and a Vehicle that hasn't been crewed yet is neither, so it isn't a legal target for the Aura spell. (Even if it had somehow been targeted and then stopped being legal, the spell would check targets on resolution and be put into its owner's graveyard for having an illegal target [608.2b], [608.3b], [608.3c].)

What Natalie should do instead: let Allen's crew ability of Capenna Express resolve. Once Capenna Express is an artifact creature, it is a legal target for One with the Stars. High Fae Trickster's ability "You may cast spells as though they had flash" lets Natalie cast One with the Stars at that instant-speed moment. If she does, One with the Stars ruling #1 applies: it may enchant a permanent that is only temporarily a creature, such as a Vehicle, and the enchanted Capenna Express becomes an enchantment and loses all other card types — permanently remaining an enchantment even after the until-end-of-turn crew effect would have expired. It keeps its abilities but is no longer a creature or artifact, so it can't attack.

Timing assumption: I'm reading the question as Natalie casting One with the Stars while the crew ability is still on the stack. If instead she casts it after the crew ability has already resolved, the paragraph above applies and Capenna Express becomes a permanent enchantment.

Number of players doesn't matter here — nothing in this interaction involves choosing a defending player or per-opponent effects, so it works the same in a two-player game or at a multiplayer table.

question: Nico controls [Humility]. Aitana casts [Finale of Devastation] with X = 10. Will the creature they find have haste?
answer:
Yes — the creature Aitana finds will have haste, and it will be an 11/11.

Why: both Humility and Finale of Devastation create continuous effects that are sorted by CR 613 layers, and within a layer by timestamp (CR 613.1). Humility says "All creatures lose all abilities and have base power and toughness 1/1": the ability-removal part applies in layer 6 and the base-P/T-setting part in layer 7b (see [Humility ruling #2], which spells out that Humility's parts apply in their respective layers). Finale of Devastation, with X = 10, gives creatures you control +X/+X and haste until end of turn: the haste-granting part applies in layer 6, the +10/+10 in layer 7c.

In layer 6, Humility's removal has the earlier timestamp (it was already on the battlefield) and Finale of Devastation's grant is later, so the later effect prevails and the creature has haste (CR 113.10c). Humility is a continuous ability-removal effect, not a "can't have abilities" effect (CR 113.11), so it doesn't stop haste from being added afterward — it only strips abilities that existed when it applied.

P/T: layer 7b sets base 1/1 (Humility), then layer 7c adds +10/+10 (Finale of Devastation) = 11/11.

Timing note: this assumes Humility was already on the battlefield when Finale of Devastation resolved, which is what the question describes. If Humility instead entered after Finale of Devastation resolved, Humility's layer-6 removal would then be the later timestamp and would strip the granted haste (CR 113.10c). Also note per [Finale of Devastation ruling #2] and [Finale of Devastation ruling #0] that the creature just put onto the battlefield does get the +X/+X and haste, with no window for players to act in between. Haste means the creature ignores the "summoning sickness" rule, so it can attack and use {T}/untap abilities right away (CR 702.10c, CR 302.6).

Player count doesn't matter here — nothing in this interaction depends on the number of opponents; Humility affects all creatures and Finale of Devastation affects only Aitana's creatures either way.

question: Avery's [Unlicensed Hearse] has exiled five cards, and they activate its crew ability. After that resolves, Avery casts [Dress Down]. What does Unlicensed Hearse look like?
answer:
Unlicensed Hearse becomes a 0/0 colorless artifact creature Vehicle with no abilities, and it's immediately put into Avery's graveyard as a state-based action (unless something else is boosting its toughness).

Why: crewing Unlicensed Hearse makes it an artifact creature Vehicle until end of turn (layer 4). Dress Down says "Creatures lose all abilities," a layer 6 effect that applies to Unlicensed Hearse because it is currently a creature. That strips everything, including Crew 2 and the characteristic-defining ability "Unlicensed Hearse's power and toughness are each equal to the number of cards exiled with it." Since that P/T-defining ability is gone before layer 7a is reached and it hadn't started applying in any earlier layer, it never sets the power and toughness (CR 613.6 is what keeps an already-applying effect going; here it never started). With no P/T-setting effect at all, Unlicensed Hearse is 0/0 — exactly the situation described in Unlicensed Hearse ruling #0, where a crewed Hearse with no exiled cards dies as a 0/0. Losing the creature type isn't what happens here — it stays a creature, it just has no abilities.

Note it keeps the five cards in exile; if Dress Down is later sacrificed at the beginning of the end step, a Hearse that somehow survived would be 5/5 again. But it won't survive: state-based actions are checked as soon as a player would get priority after Dress Down resolves, so it goes to the graveyard first. Per Dress Down ruling #0, only abilities it has while Dress Down is on the battlefield are lost — abilities granted afterward would stick, but that doesn't save the printed CDA here.

Timing assumption: Avery crewed first and Dress Down resolved afterward. If instead Dress Down were already on the battlefield and Avery then tried to crew, Unlicensed Hearse would have no Crew 2 ability to activate at all (it isn't a creature yet, so it keeps abilities until it becomes one — but crewing it is what makes it a creature, and once it is, it's a 0/0 that dies the same way).

This works identically in two-player and multiplayer games; nothing here depends on the number of players.

question: Alex controls [Karametra, God of Harvests], and then casts [Opalescence]. Their devotion to white is 2. Is Karametra, God of Harvests a creature? If so, what is its power and toughness?
answer:
Yes — Karametra, God of Harvests is a creature, and it's a 5/5.

Why:

1. Devotion. Karametra, God of Harvests' own ability turns off the creature type only while your devotion to green and white is less than seven. Karametra, God of Harvests' mana cost {3}{G}{W} contributes {G} and {W} (2), and Opalescence's mana cost {2}{W}{W} contributes 2 more white symbols, so devotion to green and white is at most 4 here — well under seven. So that ability is active. (Note {3} and {2} are generic mana and count for nothing; only colored symbols count.)

2. Layer 4 (type-changing), applied in timestamp order (CR 613.2, 613.2a for the copiable sublayer; timestamps govern within a layer). Karametra, God of Harvests was already on the battlefield, so its type-changing effect has the earlier timestamp and applies first: Karametra, God of Harvests stops being a creature and loses the creature type God, remaining a legendary enchantment (Karametra, God of Harvests ruling #15). Then Opalescence, with the later timestamp, applies: Karametra, God of Harvests is now a non-Aura enchantment other than Opalescence, so Opalescence makes it a creature in addition to its other types. Net result at the end of layer 4: it IS a creature (an enchantment creature with no creature subtype, since God was already stripped).

question: Autumn animates [Inkmoth Nexus] and attacks with it. Nayeli then flashes in [Dress Down]. What does Inkmoth Nexus look like?
answer:
Inkmoth Nexus is a colorless 1/1 Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature land with NO abilities — no flying, no infect, and no mana ability — and it's still attacking.

How it gets there, layer by layer (CR 613.6, 613.7):

- Layer 4 (types): Autumn's activation of Inkmoth Nexus's ability makes it an artifact creature Phyrexian Blinkmoth that's still a land; it keeps its prior land type line (CR 205.1b).
- Layer 6 (abilities), timestamp order: first Inkmoth Nexus's animation grants flying and infect; then Nayeli's Dress Down (later timestamp) applies "Creatures lose all abilities." Since Inkmoth Nexus is a creature at this point, it loses everything — the granted flying and infect, and its own printed "{T}: Add {C}" and "{1}:" animation abilities.
- Layer 7b (set P/T): the animation's "becomes a 1/1" part still applies. Under CR 613.6, once an effect has started applying, it keeps applying in each later applicable layer even though the ability generating it was removed in layer 6. So Inkmoth Nexus is 1/1, not 0/0, and it does not die.

Practical consequences: Inkmoth Nexus deals normal combat damage now, not poison counters, because infect is gone (CR 113.12 — losing a granted ability is exactly what Dress Down does). It also can't be tapped for {C} while Dress Down is out. Removing Dress Down later in the turn brings back the printed abilities and the granted flying/infect for the rest of the turn, since the animation effect is still running.

Timing assumption: I'm assuming Dress Down was flashed in after Inkmoth Nexus was already animated and attacking (as stated). If instead Dress Down were already on the battlefield before Autumn activated the ability, Autumn couldn't activate it at all — Inkmoth Nexus would be a land with no abilities to activate.

Player count doesn't change any of this; the layer system works identically in two-player and multiplayer games. The only multiplayer wrinkle is which opponent Inkmoth Nexus is attacking, which the provided rules don't bear on.

question: In their first main phase, Alexandra activates [Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance] to create two tokens, and Nehemiah responds with [Dress Down]. What happens with the tokens?
answer:
The two 1/1 colorless Spirit creature tokens are still created, and they still have haste.

Details:

1. Dress Down resolving first doesn't stop the tokens. Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance's channel ability exists on the stack independently of its source once activated, so it resolves normally and creates the tokens [113.7a]. Nothing here says a permanent with those characteristics can't enter, so rule 111.5 (which prevents token creation in that case) doesn't apply.

2. The tokens keep haste. Dress Down says "Creatures lose all abilities," but that only strips abilities the creature has as of Dress Down's effect; an ability granted to a creature after Dress Down entered the battlefield is not removed [Dress Down ruling #0]. Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance's ability creates the tokens and grants them haste until end of turn at the moment they're created, which is after Dress Down entered, so the haste-granting effect has the later timestamp and applies on top of Dress Down [Dress Down ruling #0]. The tokens have no other printed abilities to lose anyway, so functionally they are 1/1 hasty Spirits and can attack this turn.

3. Timing assumption: I'm assuming Nehemiah cast Dress Down in response, so Dress Down resolves before the Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance channel ability. If instead Dress Down somehow resolved after the tokens were already on the battlefield with haste, Dress Down would then be the later effect and would strip haste from those tokens (and all other creatures) while it remains on the battlefield.

4. Cost note: the channel cost is {3}{R} plus discarding Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance, reduced by {1} generic for each legendary creature Alexandra controls; the {R} is never reduced.

5. Player count: nothing in this interaction depends on the number of players, so the result is the same in a two-player game or at a multiplayer table.

question: Aubree casts [Blood Moon]. Nikolas activates [Inkmoth Nexus]'s ability in response. What will Inkmoth Nexus look like after everything resolves? What will it look like next turn?
answer:
For the rest of this turn, Inkmoth Nexus is a 1/1 colorless artifact land creature — Mountain Phyrexian Blinkmoth with flying, infect, and "{T}: Add {R}" (note: {R} is red mana specifically; it no longer taps for {C}, colorless mana). Next turn, once the activated ability's "until end of turn" effect has worn off, it's just a land — Mountain with "{T}: Add {R}" and nothing else, as long as Blood Moon remains on the battlefield.

Why: Nikolas's activated ability resolves first (earlier timestamp), then Blood Moon resolves. In layer 4 (type-changing, CR 613.1d), the Inkmoth Nexus ability adds Artifact and Creature types plus the creature types Phyrexian Blinkmoth and keeps Land (CR 205.1b, "It's still a land"). Blood Moon then sets its land subtype to Mountain; per CR 305.7 that replaces land types only, so the creature types Phyrexian and Blinkmoth stay, and no card types or supertypes are added or removed (Blood Moon ruling #1 — it also doesn't change the name or make it basic).

In layer 6 (CR 613.1f, timestamp order per CR 613.3/613.7), the Inkmoth Nexus effect grants flying and infect; then Blood Moon, via CR 305.7, strips the abilities generated by Inkmoth Nexus's own rules text ("{T}: Add {C}" and the {1} animation ability) and grants "{T}: Add {R}" (Blood Moon ruling #2). Crucially, CR 305.7 says this doesn't remove abilities granted by other effects, so flying and infect survive.

In layer 7b the power/toughness-setting part of the already-applying Inkmoth Nexus effect still makes it 1/1 — CR 613.6: an effect that started applying in one layer keeps applying in later layers even though the ability generating it was removed in the meantime.

Timing note: I'm assuming the ability was activated and resolved before Blood Moon resolved, as stated. If instead Blood Moon had already resolved first, the {1} ability would be gone and couldn't be activated at all — Inkmoth Nexus would simply be a Mountain. Nothing here depends on the number of players; the answer is the same in two-player and multiplayer games.

question: Niko controls [Urza's Saga] on chapter 2. Ainsley casts [Magus of the Moon]. What happens to Urza's Saga?
answer:
Urza's Saga is immediately sacrificed. Magus of the Moon's static ability "Nonbasic lands are Mountains" applies in layer 4 (type-changing effects) and sets Urza's Saga's land subtype to Mountain [613.1d]. Per rule 305.7, when an effect sets a land's subtype to a basic land type, the land loses its old land types and loses all abilities generated from its rules text, and gains the mana ability for the new type — so Urza's Saga loses its three chapter abilities (and the "{2}, {T}: Create a Construct" ability it had gained from chapter II) and instead has just "{T}: Add {R}" [305.6][Mountain].

Crucially, Magus of the Moon changes only land subtypes; it doesn't touch card types or supertypes [305.7][Magus of the Moon ruling #1]. Urza's Saga is an "Enchantment Land — Urza's Saga," so it remains an enchantment with the Saga subtype (that's an enchantment subtype, not a land type) while now also being a Mountain. That's exactly the case covered by [Urza's Saga ruling #1]: if Urza's Saga loses all of its chapter abilities but is still a Saga, perhaps due to a card like Blood Moon, it is immediately sacrificed. Magus of the Moon has the same effect as Blood Moon here, so Niko sacrifices Urza's Saga as a state-based action the moment Magus of the Moon is on the battlefield — Niko never gets to use the Construct-making ability.

Note also that Magus of the Moon's effect applies in layer 4 before ability-removal effects are considered, so even if Magus of the Moon itself later loses its abilities, nonbasic lands keep being Mountains [Magus of the Moon ruling #0].

Timing assumption: Magus of the Moon must resolve and be on the battlefield for its static ability to apply — while Magus of the Moon is still on the stack, Urza's Saga is unaffected, and Niko can respond by activating the chapter II ability (paying {2} and tapping) to make a Construct token before Magus of the Moon resolves.

This works identically at any table size; nothing here depends on the number of players, since Magus of the Moon affects all nonbasic lands regardless of controller.

question: Nico controls [Dress Down], and Aya activates [Inkmoth Nexus]. What does it look like?
answer:
Aya's Inkmoth Nexus becomes a 1/1 colorless Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact land creature that DOES have flying and infect, even though Nico's Dress Down says "Creatures lose all abilities."

Why: continuous effects are applied in layers (CR 613.1), and one effect can have parts in several layers (CR 613.6).
- Layer 4 (types): Inkmoth Nexus's activated ability makes it an artifact creature — Phyrexian Blinkmoth — and it's still a land, keeping all prior card types (CR 205.1b).
- Layer 6 (abilities): Dress Down has the earlier timestamp (it was already on the battlefield), so it applies first and strips everything — including Inkmoth Nexus's "{T}: Add {C}" mana ability and its own "{1}:" animation ability. Then the already-resolved animation effect applies its later-timestamped part, granting flying and infect. Under CR 613.6, once that effect started applying (in layer 4), it keeps applying in every other layer even though the ability that generated it has been removed.
- Layer 7b: power and toughness are set to 1/1.

So the net result is a 1/1 flying, infect artifact land creature that can no longer tap for {C} and can't be animated again while Dress Down is out (its {1} ability is gone). If Dress Down leaves later this turn, Inkmoth Nexus gets its printed abilities back and remains a 1/1 flier with infect for the rest of the turn.

Timing assumption: I'm assuming Dress Down was already on the battlefield when Aya activated Inkmoth Nexus. If instead Aya activates and resolves the ability first and Nico then plays Dress Down, the outcome is the same by timestamp order anyway — Dress Down would then be the later effect in layer 6 and would strip flying and infect too, leaving a 1/1 land creature with no abilities at all. (Dress Down is the later timestamp in that case, so that is the meaningful difference: flying/infect are stripped.)

Player count doesn't matter here; nothing in this interaction depends on the number of players.

question: Avery enchants their [Hall] with [Unbridled Growth]. Next turn, Nickolas casts [Blood Moon]. What colors of mana can Hall tap for?
answer:
Hall can still tap for any one color — white, blue, black, red, or green — because Unbridled Growth's granted mana ability survives Blood Moon.

Why: Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains." Under CR 305.7, setting a land's subtype to a basic land type makes it lose its old land types and all abilities generated from its rules text, and it gains the intrinsic ability of the new basic land type — for Mountain, "{T}: Add {R}" (CR 305.6, Blood Moon ruling #2). But CR 305.7 explicitly states this "doesn't remove any abilities that were granted to the land by other effects." Unbridled Growth's "Enchanted land has '{T}: Add one mana of any color'" is exactly such a granted ability (CR 113.12 — an effect that gives an object an ability is a grant, distinct from setting a characteristic).

Working it through the layers (CR 613.9 for how the effects stack): in layer 4 Blood Moon sets Hall's subtype to Mountain; in layer 6 Unbridled Growth (earlier timestamp) adds the any-color ability, then Blood Moon strips Hall's printed abilities ("This land enters tapped," "{T}: Add {R} or {W}," and the {4}, {T}: Investigate ability) and adds "{T}: Add {R}." End result: Hall is a land with subtype Mountain whose only abilities are "{T}: Add one mana of any color" and "{T}: Add {R}."

So Hall taps for any single color of your choice (the {R} ability is redundant), but it can only be tapped once — both are {T} abilities. Note it has lost the {4}, {T}: Investigate ability and the enters-tapped clause.

If Unbridled Growth is later destroyed or sacrificed ("Sacrifice this Aura: Draw a card"), Hall goes back to producing only {R}. This answer is the same regardless of the number of players at the table; nothing here depends on player count.

cited_text.113.12: An effect that sets an object’s characteristic, or simply states a quality of that object, is different from an ability granted by an effect. When an object “gains” or “has” an ability, that ability can be removed by another effect. If an effect defines a characteristic of the object (“[permanent] is [characteristic value]”), it’s not granting an ability. (See rule 604.3.) Similarly, if an effect states a quality of that object (“[creature] can’t be blocked,” for example), it’s neither granting an ability nor setting a characteristic. Muraganda Petroglyphs reads, “Creatures with no abilities get +2/+2.” A Runeclaw Bear (a creature with no abilities) enchanted by an Aura that says “Enchanted creature has flying” would not get +2/+2. A Runeclaw Bear enchanted by an Aura that says “Enchanted creature is red” or “Enchanted creature can’t be blocked” would get +2/+2.
cited_text.613.9: One continuous effect can override another. Sometimes the results of one effect determine whether another effect applies or what another effect does. Two effects are affecting the same creature: one from an Aura that says “Enchanted creature has flying” and one from an Aura that says “Enchanted creature loses flying.” Neither of these depends on the other, since nothing changes what they affect or what they’re doing to it. Applying them in timestamp order means the one that was generated last “wins.” The same process would be followed, and the same result reached, if either of the effects had a duration (such as “Target creature loses flying until end of turn”) or came from a non-Aura source (such as “All creatures lose flying”). One effect reads, “White creatures get +1/+1,” and another reads, “Enchanted creature is white.” The enchanted creature gets +1/+1 from the first effect, regardless of its previous color.
